security_audit.summary: All 13 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code spans, code fences, an informational URL, and a relative documentation link. The embedded example still presents two medium risks: unescaped user input in HTML email and a publicly callable email-sending flow without explicit abuse controls. These example patterns should be hardened before publication.

remediation.issue: The example concatenates the user-provided name directly into an HTML email body.
remediation.suggestion: Escape or sanitize all user-controlled values before inserting them into HTML email content.

remediation.issue: The public registration example sends email without documented rate limits or cooldowns.
remediation.suggestion: Require an appropriate identity, validate addresses, and add per-caller and per-address rate limits before sending email.

content.user_title: Add Email Verification to Caffeine AI Apps
content.value_statement: Unverified addresses can weaken account trust and communication. This skill guides Caffeine AI developers through click-to-verify flows using supported Motoko modules.
actual_capabilities: Guides integration of the prefabricated verified email state module.
Shows how to include the verification callback mixin in a Motoko actor.
Explains how to send recipient-specific messages with a verification URL placeholder.
Provides a registration example with caller and email uniqueness checks.
Shows how to query whether the current user's email is verified.
Reminds admin interface builders to preserve the required verification URL placeholder.
limitations: Requires the Caffeine AI email extension and compatible Motoko packages.
Provides instructions and examples, not a standalone verification service.
Uses prefabricated verification modules that the application cannot modify.
The sample lacks HTML escaping, address validation, and explicit rate limiting.

use_cases.title: Verify New Accounts
use_cases.description: Add ownership confirmation to a Motoko registration flow before enabling trusted account actions.

use_cases.title: Track Verified Addresses
use_cases.description: Use the supported state module to check verified status without duplicating profile fields.

use_cases.title: Prepare Verification Templates
use_cases.description: Build admin-managed email content that keeps the required verification URL placeholder.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up Verification
prompt_templates.prompt: Add email verification to my Caffeine AI Motoko app. Show the required imports, state initialization, and callback mixin.

prompt_templates.title: Send a Verification Message
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a verification email flow for new users. Include the required URL placeholder and handle the send result.

prompt_templates.title: Build Registration Checks
prompt_templates.prompt: Design registration and verified-status endpoints. Prevent duplicate callers and duplicate addresses while using the supported verified email store.

prompt_templates.title: Harden the Verification Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my verification design for abuse risks. Add input validation, HTML escaping, rate limits, and tests while preserving the supported modules.

output_examples.input: Add verification to a new Motoko actor.
output_examples.output: A backend plan covering package imports, verified-address state, callback mixin inclusion, email sending, and a verified-status query.

output_examples.input: Create a safe registration email flow.
output: Validate and normalize the submitted address.
Escape the display name before building HTML.
Send one message containing the required verification URL placeholder.
Handle delivery errors and apply request limits.

output_examples.input: Explain how verified status should be stored.
output_examples.output: Use the prefabricated verified email state and its contains function. Do not duplicate verification status in user profiles.

best_practices: Use the supported verified email store as the single source of verification status.
Keep the verification URL placeholder in every HTML template sent through the extension.
Validate addresses, escape HTML values, and rate-limit verification requests.
anti_patterns: Do not store a separate verification flag on each user profile.
Do not remove or alter the required verification URL placeholder.
Do not place unescaped user input directly into an HTML email.

faq.question: What does this skill verify?
faq.answer: It supports proof that a recipient controls an email address by using a recipient-specific verification link.

faq.question: Which platform does it target?
faq.answer: It targets Caffeine AI applications written in Motoko.

faq.question: Which dependency sends the email?
faq.answer: The separate Caffeine AI email extension provides the sendVerificationEmail function.

faq.question: Where is verified status stored?
faq.answer: The prefabricated verifiedEmails module stores verified addresses and provides the contains function.

faq.question: What must every email template include?
faq.answer: The HTML body must include the VERIFICATION_URL placeholder for the recipient-specific link.

faq.question: Is the sample ready for production?
faq.answer: No. Add input validation, HTML escaping, rate limits, monitoring, and tests before production use.
